review_note: Independent comparison against pinned original theorem in Stage A sites.tex:10902; no proof or unsafe raw slice viewed. For any object U in a category, sieves are subfunctors of h_U, hence form a set ordered by inclusion. The source also asserts closure under unions and intersections, existence of the generated sieve, and maximal/minimal sieves h_U and ∅; all six items and the uniqueness qualifier are separately preserved.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The collection of sieves on $U$ is a set.
\item Inclusion defines a partial ordering on this set.
\item Unions and intersections of sieves are sieves.
\item
\label{item-sieve-generated}
Given a family of morphisms $\{U_i \to U\}_{i\in I}$
of $\mathcal{C}$ with target $U$
there exists a unique smallest sieve $S$ on $U$ such that
each $U_i \to U$ belongs to $S(U_i)$.
\item The sieve $S = h_U$ is the maximal sieve.
\item The empty subpresheaf is the minimal sieve.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions: The collection of sieves on $U$ is a set.
Inclusion defines a partial ordering on this set.
Unions and intersections of sieves are sieves.

review_note: Independent comparison against pinned original theorem in Stage A sites.tex:11014; no proof or unsafe raw slice viewed. For Grothendieck topology J, covering sieves at U are closed under finite intersection and upward under inclusion. The only conditional hypothesis, S∈J(U) and S'⊇S, correctly applies to the second numbered conclusion, not the unconditional first.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $J$ be a topology on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Finite intersections of elements of $J(U)$ are in $J(U)$.
\item If $S \in J(U)$ and $S' \supset S$, then $S' \in J(U)$.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: Finite intersections of elements of $J(U)$ are in $J(U)$.

review_note: Independent comparison against pinned original theorem in Stage A sites.tex:11065; no proof or unsafe raw slice viewed. The intersection of a set-indexed family of Grothendieck topologies is again a topology. The lattice of topologies also has a least common upper bound, expressed as a coarsest topology finer than every J_i. Both independent assertions match the source.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\{J_i\}_{i\in I}$ be a set of topologies.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The rule $J(U) = \bigcap J_i(U)$ defines
a topology on $\mathcal{C}$.
\item There is a coarsest topology finer than
all of the topologies $J_i$.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: Independent comparison against pinned original theorem in Stage A sites.tex:11113; no proof or unsafe raw slice viewed. The covering sieves are exactly those whose pullbacks to each V→U are local bijections when mapped into every chosen presheaf F_i. This construction yields the finest Grothendieck topology on C for which all F_i are sheaves, preserving the universal 'every V→U and all i' condition.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $\{ \mathcal{F}_i \}_{i\in I}$ be a
collection of presheaves of sets on $\mathcal{C}$. For each
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ denote
$J(U)$ the set of sieves $S$ on $U$ with the following property:
For every morphism $V \to U$, the maps
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(h_V, \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(S \times_U V, \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
are bijective for all $i \in I$. Then $J$ defines a
topology on $\mathcal{C}$. This topology is the finest
topology in which all of the $\mathcal{F}_i$ are sheaves.

\label{lemma-topology-presheaves-sheaves}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $\{ \mathcal{F}_i \}_{i\in I}$ be a
collection of presheaves of sets on $\mathcal{C}$. For each
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ denote
$J(U)$ the set of sieves $S$ on $U$ with the following property:
For every morphism $V \to U$, the maps
$$
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(h_V, \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(S \times_U V, \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
are bijective for all $i \in I$. Then $J$ defines a
topology on $\mathcal{C}$. This topology is the finest
topology in which all of the $\mathcal{F}_i$ are sheaves.
